'''Yuri Estrin''' (professor), also written "Juri Estrin", is an international authority on [[materials science]] and [[engineering]], particularly in the areas of [[physical metallurgy]], [[materials modelling]], and development of new materials.<ref name=csiro>{{cite web|url=http://www.csiro.au/people/Yuri.Estrin.html|title=Professor Yuri Estrin: excellence in the area of physical metallurgy|date=18 January 2010}}</ref> He is a [[list of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]]<ref name="Australian Academy of Science">{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/professor-yuri-estrin|title=Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science}}</ref> and recipient of an honorary doctorate from the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 2008.<ref name=RAS>{{cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/viewnumbereddoc.aspx?id=cae214f9-626d-4be1-9d92-6f48602d1294&_Language=ru|title=Yuri Estrin awarded Honorary Doctorate by Russian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> In 2015, he won a [[Thomson Reuters]] Australian Citation Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.com.au/m/pdf/PR_CIA_2015.pdf|title=Thomson Reuters 2015 Citation Award}}</ref>
Yuri Estrin was born and educated in the former [[Soviet Union]], where he completed his university studies in Physics and Materials Engineering in [[Moscow]] with a high distinction.<ref name=csiro/>

He worked as a researcher at the Institute of Crystallography of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]] and received his [[PhD degree]] from that institution in 1975.

In 1977, he briefly visited Germany as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]]. After leaving the Soviet Union in the [[Leonid Brezhnev]] years, Estrin migrated to Germany and ultimately moved to [[Hamburg]] in 1981 with his wife, Karin Estrin.

In Hamburg, at the newly established University of Technology ([[TUHH]]), he received his [[habilitation]] and became professor of physical metallurgy. His son [[Daniel Estrin]], was also born in Hamburg.

Estrin and his family migrated to [[Western Australia]] in 1992, where he became professor in the Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering at the [[University of Western Australia]].<ref name=csiro/>

Since then, Estrin has held the chair in Physical Metallurgy at [[Clausthal University of Technology]] in Germany and joined the Department of Materials Engineering at [[Monash University]] in [[Melbourne]] as Professor and later Director of the Centre for Advanced Hybrid Materials. He is currently an Honorary Professorial Fellow in this department.

Yuri Estrin has received international recognition for his scientific achievements, including [[Humboldt Award]]s (1999 and 2012),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.monash.edu/news/articles/nanotechnology-researcher-honoured |title=Nanotechnology researcher honoured |publisher=[[Monash University]] |date=20 April 2012 |access-date=7 November 2018}}</ref> a Staudinger-Durrer Lecture at the [[Swiss Federal University of Technology]] (2011), a World-Class University professorship at [[Seoul National University]] (2009-2013), and a Helmholtz International Fellow Award from the [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.helmholtz.de/print/aktuell/presseinformationen/pressearchiv/artikel/artikeldetail/forschung_ueber_grenzen_hinaus_helmholtz_international_fellow_awards_verliehen/|title=Forschung ueber Grenzen hinaus}}</ref> Estrin is also an adjunct professor at the [[Pohang University of Science and Technology]] (Korea) and [[Nanjing University of Science and Technology]] (China). In 2013, he won a grant of the Russian government under the so-called 'megagrant' scheme to establish research activities in hybrid nanostructured materials at [[Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys]]. He was awarded an Honorary Doctorate from the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (2008) and was elected [[list of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] (2013).<ref name="Australian Academy of Science"/>

Estrin is the author of more than 500 publications focussing on [[nanomaterials]] including [[nanomechanics]], [[light alloys]], [[alloy design]], [[thin films]], [[hybrid materials]] and [[multimaterials]] as well as design of novel materials based on [[geometry principles]].

Estrin's daughter, Prof. [[Masha Niv]], is an academic working in the area of [[bioinformatics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nano.monash.edu.au/case-studies/yuri-estrin.html|title=Professor Yuri Estrin}}</ref>
